boundary_evidence: PARTIAL RUN, 31 of 52. tools/tu_map.py calls 0x020e3854..0x020e6bf4 one contiguous linker run of 52 function(s) (build/tu_map.json), and queue_audit.py extends it over the zero-gap factory dScMgCurling2_c_classInit at 0x020e6bf4 for 53 in a 0x020e3854..0x020e6c28 span. This TU licenses 0x020e3854..0x020e5450, 31 function(s), ROM ordinals 0..30. The other 21 keep their own shards and their own delinks.txt entries; the 22nd is the sourceless hole in EDGE 1 below, which has neither.

EDGE 1 -- a sourceless hole splits the run, and it is the only edge. ROM ordinal 31, func_ov006_020e5450 (0x020e5450, size 0x560), has no source anywhere in the tree: it carries a symbols.txt row but NO src/ file and NO entry in config/arm9/overlays/ov006/delinks.txt at all (the blocks jump from 0x020e513c-0x020e5450 straight to 0x020e59b0), so the cartridge's own bytes cover that range. It is a banked near-miss whose best recorded attempt sits at 29 divergences (config/match_attempts.jsonl). It sits in the MIDDLE of the run, and no delink block and no TU manifest in this tree expresses a .text claim with a hole in it, so the run can only be licensed as one of its two contiguous sides.

WHY THE LOWER SIDE. This TU is the larger side by member count: 31 below the hole against 21 above it. It is also the side that holds the class's key function -- the destructor, which include/dScMgCurling2_c.h declares out of line and declares FIRST -- so it is the side that can emit and license the class's _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS. It is the larger side in bytes too: 0x1bfc against the upper side's 0x1278. The upper side holds four of the six own vtable overrides (InitResources, Behavior, Render, OnYoshiTryEat) and the classInit factory, but not the key function, so a promotion there would carry compiler_only_output: 0 -- the dScMgCoin_c outcome -- and would leave the destructor pair enrolled as shards.

The class's own vtable, emitted because this TU owns the key function. Extent corroborated three ways, per notes/agents/roles/writer.md: (a) the relocated run in config/arm9/overlays/ov006/relocs.txt is unbroken from 0x0213c50c (the typeinfo word of the 8-byte offset-to-top/typeinfo preamble) through 0x0213c59c, with the first gap at 0x0213c5a0 and the next relocation not until 0x0213c5c8; (b) tools/rtti_vtables.py --own dScMgCurling2_c reports 36 slots (base dScMgBase_c also 36, six of them overridden: slots 0, 6, 9, 16, 17, 18); (c) the next symbols.txt row after the address point is data_ov006_0213c5a0 at 0x0213c5a0. All three give symbol extent 0x0213c510..0x0213c5a0 = 0x90 = 36 slots, and STORAGE 0x0213c508..0x0213c5a0 = 0x98, which is exactly the size tubuild verify reports for the .data section this TU emits (EXTRA .data _ZTV15dScMgCurling2_c size=0x98). (The naive next-symbol read happens to be RIGHT here: this table's phantom interior symbol, data_ov006_0213c510, sits ON the address point rather than inside the table.) The cartridge keeps its canonical copy at ov006:0x0213c510, outside this TU's only licensed range (.text 0x020e3854-0x020e5450), so dsd delinks it from the cartridge independently and discarding this object's copy cannot cost the image a byte.

Homeless. mwcc emits three destructor variants from the one out-of-line definition -- D1, D0, D2 in that order under defer_codegen off -- but the cartridge carries only D1 (0x020e3854) and D0 (0x020e3878). dScMgCurling2_c is a confirmed leaf: no edge in build/rtti.json names it as a base, so its own D2 is never odr-used, no address anywhere in config/ names a D2 for this class and no instruction in the image calls one. It has no ROM home, so plain deadstrip rather than deadstrip-duplicate, and production isolation discards it. It is emitted AFTER D0 and before ordinal 2, so it does not disturb the licensed run's ROM-ascending emission order.

decl_common.h is deliberately NOT included. It declares nine of this TU's 31 members (func_ov006_020e38b0, 020e3948, 020e3bc4, 020e4800, 020e4a84, 020e4b78, 020e4fe8, 020e507c as `void*`/`int` and 020e48d4 as `char*`), and eight of the nine contradict the byte-matched shard. Including it would raise `illegal function overloading` against code that already matches. Precedent: ov006/dScMgPanel_c, ov002/Player.

func_ov006_020e4b00 and func_ov006_020e4ed4 each spelled their receiver parameter `this`, which mwccarm 2004/b56 rejects in a C++ TU; both were renamed to `self`. func_ov006_020e4ed4 has since become dScMgCurling2_c::DragBegin, so its receiver really is `this` again.

METHOD-CONVERSION PASS (stage 3.5). Seventeen of the 29 non-destructor members are now real dScMgCurling2_c:: methods declared in include/dScMgCurling2_c.h: SpawnValue, StepYRampDown, StepYRampUp, StepYRestart, StepXSettle, StepXPushNeg, StepXPushPos, StepXPick, StepXAndY, StepXSettleFast, StepXPushNegFast, StepXPushPosFast, StepXPickFast, StepXOnly, PickStepMode, DragUpdate and DragBegin. Every conversion is byte-neutral: 31/31 MATCH, objisolate clean, ROM-ascending emission order, unchanged from the pre-conversion run. The bodies keep the shard's raw-offset spellings behind a `char *x = (char *)this;` prologue, so none of the humanizer's measured levers moved.

SYMBOLS.TXT IS PART OF THIS EDIT. Sixteen of the seventeen renamed members are the target of an 8-byte {code pointer, zero adjustment} pointer-to-member record in unowned ov006 .data (0x0213c40c..0x0213c4b4), which __sinit_ov006_02130758 copies into the BSS dispatch arrays. dsd resolves those records BY SYMBOL NAME, so all seventeen rows in config/arm9/overlays/ov006/symbols.txt move to the mangled spelling in the same commit; a row left behind would link its .data code word as 0x00000000 with a green compile. SpawnValue is the seventeenth: it carries no .data record and is reached only from inside this TU and from the sourceless hole's own cartridge bytes.

TWELVE MEMBERS REFUSED CONVERSION, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED AND IS NOT BYTES. With all 29 converted the TU still reports 31/31 MATCH / objisolate clean / ROM-ascending, but `python tools/rombuild.py -j 6 --no-rom` fails with exactly twelve `mwldarm.exe: Undefined` lines: func_ov006_020e38b0, _020e3948, _020e3bc4, _020e4a84, _020e4b78, _020e4fe8, _020e507c (referenced from dScMgCurling2_c::Render()), _020e4800 and _020e3948 (Behavior()), _020e48d4 (InitResources()), _020e3b9c (func_ov006_020e668c), _020e4b00 (func_ov006_020e628c) and _020e513c (func_ov006_020e5e3c). Those callers are still one-function shards above the sourceless hole, and they -- and include/decl_common.h -- spell the target by its C name. The twelve convert byte-neutrally the day segment B is promoted; nothing else blocks them.

THE SEVENTEEN NAMES ARE COINED. The ROM proves member-ness (a zero-adjustment pointer-to-member record) and each handler's index in its own table, both read out of __sinit_ov006_02130758 and quoted in include/dScMgCurling2_c.h. It does not carry the original identifiers, and the gameplay semantics of the 0x48c0 and 0x4fe0 record arrays remain on the scout's `unproven` list; no name asserts them.
